hints: For each query [l,r], count distinct values in that range.
Sweep r from left to right and keep a marker only at each value's latest occurrence.
When a new occurrence appears, remove the old marker; a Fenwick range sum then counts latest occurrences inside [l,r].
analogy: At the current right boundary, each value leaves one token at its newest position; a query sees exactly the values represented in its interval.
example: For array 1,2,1 at right=3, markers are at positions 2 and 3; query [2,3] sees two distinct values.
algorithm: Sort queries by right endpoint. Advance a sweep, update Fenwick latest-position markers, and answer each query by sum(l..r).
correctness: A value has a marker in [l,r] exactly when its latest occurrence up to r is in that range, which is equivalent to occurring somewhere in [l,r].
complexity: O((n+q) log n) time and O(n+q) space.
